남자.x: That man is my older brother.

김치.x: This kimchi is a bit spicy.
김치.e: Probably from an old word meaning 'soaked vegetables'.

모자.x: The sun was strong, so I wore a hat.
모자.e: 모 (hat) + 자, a common noun ending.
모자.t: Hats and glasses use 쓰다: 모자를 쓰다, 안경을 쓰다.

가수.ex: 저는 그 가수의 노래를 정말 좋아해요.
가수.x: I really like that singer's songs.
가수.e: Literally 'song hand' — 수 marks a skilled person.

편지.x: I wrote a letter to my parents.
편지.e: Sino-Korean, but the parts don't add up; 지 = paper, as in 휴지 (tissue).
편지.t: 편지 is a letter you send, not a letter of the alphabet (글자).

뉴스.x: My father watches the news every morning.

여권.x: Please show your passport at the airport.
여권.t: Pronounced [여꿘] with a tense ㄲ sound.

살다.forms: 살아요 · 살았어요 · 살 거예요 · 사세요 (ㄹ drops)
살다.e: 삶 (life) comes from 살다. 서울에 살아요 = I live in Seoul.
살다.t: Both 서울에서 살아요 and 서울에 살아요 are correct. 어디 사세요? = Where do you live?

친절하다.x: The staff at that store are really friendly.

내다.m: to pay; to put out, to hand in
내다.e: Related to 나다 'come out': the basic idea is making something come out, like money.
내다.t: "제가 낼게요" ("I'll pay") and "제가 살게요" ("It's my treat") are both common when picking up a bill.

신호.ex: 빨간 신호일 때는 꼭 멈춰야 해요.
신호.x: You must stop when the light is red.
신호.t: 신호등 is the traffic light itself; 신호 is the signal it shows: 신호가 바뀌었어요.

출발.ex: 서울로 가는 기차의 출발 시간은 오후 세 시예요.
출발.x: The departure time for the train to Seoul is 3 p.m.

날씬하다.x: My older sister is tall and slim.

건조하다.ex: 겨울에는 공기가 건조해서 피부가 자주 가려워요.
건조하다.x: In winter the air is dry, so my skin often gets itchy.

신문.ex: 우리 할아버지는 매일 아침 신문을 읽으세요.
신문.x: My grandfather reads the newspaper every morning.

펴다.m: to open, to spread out, to unfold; to straighten
펴다.x: Everyone, now open your books to page 30.
펴다.t: A classic classroom phrase: 책을 펴세요 'Open your books'; also 우산을 펴다 'open an umbrella'.

바위.ex: 산 위에 아주 큰 바위가 있어요.
바위.x: There is a very big rock on top of the mountain.
바위.t: 돌 is any stone or pebble; 바위 is a big rock or boulder.

소포.x: Yesterday I sent a package home from the post office.

프라이팬.ex: 프라이팬을 충분히 달군 후에 고기를 구우세요.
프라이팬.x: Heat the frying pan well, then cook the meat.
프라이팬.t: Recipes often begin with 프라이팬에 기름을 두르다 'coat the pan with oil'.

제안하다.x: My friend suggested that we go hiking together this weekend.

제출.x: The deadline for submitting the report is tomorrow afternoon.

표시.x: I marked the important parts in red.

차별하다.ex: 나이나 성별로 사람을 차별하면 안 돼요.
차별하다.x: You shouldn't discriminate against people because of age or gender.
차별하다.e: Literally 'to treat as different and separate.'
차별하다.t: 차별 is negative unfair treatment; for neutral 'telling apart,' use 구별하다.

야단치다.x: Mom scolded my little brother for coming home late.
야단치다.e: 야단 'fuss, uproar' + 치다; 야단났다 means 'We're in big trouble!'
야단치다.t: The receiving side is 야단맞다: 선생님께 야단맞았어요 = I got scolded by the teacher.

동창회.x: I'm going to my high school reunion this weekend.
동창회.e: Literally 'same-window meeting': people who studied by the same window.

위대하다.x: King Sejong is the great king who created Hangeul.
위대하다.e: Literally 'grand and big'; reserved for historic figures and achievements.
위대하다.t: Much stronger than English 'great'; for 'a great meal' use 훌륭하다 or 최고, not 위대하다.

유리하다.ex: 외국어를 잘하면 취업할 때 아주 유리해요.
유리하다.x: Being good at a foreign language is a big advantage when job hunting.
유리하다.t: Pattern: N에 유리하다 (favorable for N). Don't confuse with 유리 'glass', a different word.

유사하다.ex: 두 회사의 제품은 디자인이 아주 유사해요.
유사하다.x: The two companies' products are very similar in design.
유사하다.t: A more formal, written word for 비슷하다; use 비슷하다 in everyday speech.

홈런.x: There was a come-from-behind home run in the last inning.
홈런.t: Pronounced [홈넌]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅁ. 'Hit a home run' is 홈런을 치다.

합격자.ex: 합격자는 다음 주 월요일에 발표할 거예요.
합격자.x: The successful candidates will be announced next Monday.
합격자.t: Pronounced [합껵짜] — tensing after ㅂ and ㄱ.

예산.x: The budget for this trip is one million won.

소외되다.m: to be alienated, to be left out, to be marginalized
소외되다.ex: 혼자 사는 노인들이 사회에서 소외되지 않도록 도와야 해요.
소외되다.x: We should help elderly people who live alone so they aren't left out of society.

응급 처치.ex: 다친 사람에게 먼저 응급 처치를 했어요.
응급 처치.x: I gave first aid to the injured person first.
응급 처치.e: Literally 'responding to an emergency' plus 'handling it'.

다운로드.ex: 이 앱은 무료로 다운로드할 수 있어요.
다운로드.x: You can download this app for free.
다운로드.t: Casually shortened to 다운: 다운받다; the native alternative is 내려받다.

불법적.ex: 그 회사는 불법적으로 개인 정보를 모았어요.
불법적.x: That company collected personal information illegally.

아픔.ex: 시간이 지나면 이별의 아픔도 조금씩 잊혀요.
아픔.x: As time passes, even the pain of a breakup slowly fades.

교활하다.ex: 동화 속 여우는 늘 교활한 동물로 나와요.
교활하다.x: In fairy tales, the fox always appears as a cunning animal.

명확히.x: We clearly defined each person's role at the meeting.

내세우다.m: to put forward, to nominate; to emphasize, to insist on; to show off
내세우다.ex: 그 회사는 저렴한 가격을 장점으로 내세워요.
내세우다.x: That company promotes its low prices as its strong point.
내세우다.e: 내다 'out' + 세우다 'to stand up': standing something at the front.
내세우다.t: 내세울 게 없다 means 'I have nothing to brag about'.

치열하다.x: Competition for jobs is very fierce these days.
치열하다.e: Literally 'blazing and fierce', like a raging fire.
치열하다.t: Classic collocation: 경쟁이 치열하다 'competition is fierce'; also 치열한 전투 'fierce battle'.

자질.x: He has the qualities of a leader.
자질.e: Literally 'natural material': the qualities you bring to a role.
자질.t: 자질 is about suitability for a role; 소질 is a natural talent for an activity.

효자.m: a devoted son, a dutiful son
효자.x: Minsu is a devoted son who calls his parents every day.
효자.t: Also used for products: 효자 상품 means a best-selling item that brings in lots of money.

오물오물.x: The baby is munching on rice in little bites.
오물오물.e: 의태어 (manner word) for a small mouth chewing with lips closed. Its dark-vowel pair 우물우물 is bigger, slower chewing, or mumbling.
오물오물.t: Pronounced [오무로물]: the ㄹ batchim links to the next vowel. The verb 오물거리다 is common, usually about children.

부처.ex: 여러 정부 부처가 함께 대책을 마련했습니다.
부처.x: Several government ministries worked out measures together.
부처.e: Literally 'ministries and offices', the two main kinds of government units.
부처.t: Homonym alert: 부처 also means Buddha, as in 부처님.

준수.x: The company stressed compliance with safety rules.
준수.t: 준수하다 is the formal version of 지키다; common on signs and in official notices.

인도주의.ex: 그 단체는 인도주의 정신에 따라 전쟁 피해자를 돕습니다.
인도주의.x: The organization helps war victims in the spirit of humanitarianism.

은하.ex: 우리 태양계는 은하의 중심에서 꽤 멀리 떨어져 있어요.
은하.x: Our solar system is quite far from the center of the galaxy.
은하.e: Literally 'silver river', the glowing band across the night sky.

심의하다.m: to deliberate, to review (a bill, application)
심의하다.x: The National Assembly is scheduled to deliberate on the budget bill tomorrow.
심의하다.t: Often pronounced [시미하다]; 의 in a non-first syllable may sound like 이.

수렴하다.m: to gather (opinions), to collect; to converge
수렴하다.ex: 정부는 국민의 의견을 수렴해서 정책을 만들었어요.
수렴하다.x: The government gathered public opinion and made the policy.
수렴하다.t: Fixed news phrase: 의견을 수렴하다 = to gather input; in math, 수렴 means convergence.

뒤처지다.m: to fall behind, to lag behind
뒤처지다.ex: 기술 변화를 따라가지 못하면 경쟁에서 뒤처질 수 있어요.
뒤처지다.x: If you can't keep up with technological change, you may fall behind the competition.
뒤처지다.e: Built from 뒤 'behind' plus 처지다 'to sag, lag.'
뒤처지다.t: Often misspelled 뒤쳐지다; the standard spelling is 뒤처지다.

현저하다.x: The birth rate has dropped markedly in recent years.
현저하다.t: News pattern: 현저히 + 줄다, 낮아지다, 증가하다.

우물 안 개구리.forms: 우물 안 개구리 같다 · 우물 안 개구리였다
우물 안 개구리.m: a frog in a well; someone with a narrow view of the world
우물 안 개구리.ex: 해외에 나가 보니 제가 우물 안 개구리였다는 걸 알았어요.
우물 안 개구리.x: When I went abroad, I realized I'd been a frog in a well.
우물 안 개구리.e: A frog in a well thinks the sky is only as big as the opening.
우물 안 개구리.t: Usually self-critical or a gentle jab: 우물 안 개구리처럼 살다 'to live with blinkers on.'

난제.ex: 새 정부는 여러 경제 난제를 해결해야 합니다.
난제.x: The new government has to solve several tough economic problems.

편집장.ex: 편집장이 기사 제목을 다시 쓰라고 했어요.
편집장.x: The editor-in-chief told me to rewrite the article's headline.
편집장.t: Pronounced [편집짱] — the ㅈ after ㅂ is tensed.

패널.m: panel, panelist (on a TV show); panel (board)
패널.ex: 오늘 토론 프로그램에는 패널 네 명이 출연했어요.
패널.x: Four panelists appeared on today's debate show.
패널.e: From English 'panel'; in Korean it often means a single panelist, not the whole group.

본능적.x: When the ball came flying, I instinctively closed my eyes.

비합리적.ex: 화가 나면 비합리적인 결정을 내리기 쉬워요.
비합리적.x: When you're angry, it's easy to make irrational decisions.
비합리적.e: Literally 'not fitting reason'. 비- = non-/un-: 비공식, 비정상.
비합리적.t: Pronounced [비함니적] — ㅂ becomes ㅁ and ㄹ becomes ㄴ through nasalization.

의술.x: As medical skill advanced, average life expectancy got longer.

신세.ex: 직장도 잃고 집도 없는 신세가 되었어요.
신세.x: I ended up in a sorry state, without a job or a home.
신세.e: Literally 'one's body in the world' — one's lot.
신세.t: Another sense: 신세를 지다 means to owe someone a favor.

호박이 넝쿨째 굴러 들어오다.forms: 호박이 넝쿨째 굴러 들어왔어요 · 호박이 넝쿨째 굴러 들어온 셈이에요
호박이 넝쿨째 굴러 들어오다.m: to have great luck fall into one's lap, to get a windfall (lit. a pumpkin rolls in, vine and all)
호박이 넝쿨째 굴러 들어오다.ex: 좋은 사위를 얻어서 호박이 넝쿨째 굴러 들어온 기분이에요.
호박이 넝쿨째 굴러 들어오다.x: Getting such a wonderful son-in-law feels like a huge stroke of luck.
호박이 넝쿨째 굴러 들어오다.e: Not just one pumpkin but the whole vine (넝쿨째), with more pumpkins on it, rolls into your house.
호박이 넝쿨째 굴러 들어오다.t: Pronounced [호바기 넝쿨째 굴러 드러오다]. Used for big, unexpected good fortune, classically when gaining a wonderful new family member or a great deal.

안읽씹.m: ignoring a message without even opening it
안읽씹.x: It's been two days and they still haven't even opened my message, so I'm a bit hurt.
안읽씹.e: 안 읽(고) 씹다 'not read and ignore'; 씹다 'to chew' is slang for ignoring someone. Compare 읽씹 'leaving on read'.
안읽씹.t: Casual/online. Pronounced [아닉씹]. In Korean messenger apps a small '1' next to your message shows it hasn't been read yet; with 안읽씹 the 1 stays there. Some people do it on purpose so they don't look like they read and ignored it.

밀수.x: Customs caught a ring trying to smuggle gold bars.
밀수.e: Literally 'secret transport'; short for 밀수출입, secret export and import.

허무주의.ex: 그는 전쟁을 겪은 후 깊은 허무주의에 빠졌어요.
허무주의.x: After going through the war, he fell into deep nihilism.
허무주의.t: The everyday adjective is 허무하다: 인생이 허무해요 (Life feels empty).

세례.ex: 아기는 다음 주 일요일에 성당에서 세례를 받을 거예요.
세례.x: The baby will be baptized at the Catholic church next Sunday.
세례.t: Also figurative: 질문 세례를 받다 means 'to face a barrage of questions'.

멸종위기종.x: The tiger is a typical endangered species.
멸종위기종.e: Literally 'species in a crisis of extinction'.
멸종위기종.t: Pronounced [멸쫑위기종] — ㅈ after ㄹ is tensed in Sino-Korean words.

본관.m: clan seat, ancestral home of a family name
본관.ex: 같은 김씨라도 본관이 다를 수 있어요.
본관.x: Even people with the same surname Kim can have different clan seats.
본관.e: The place your clan's founder came from, e.g., 김해 김씨.
본관.t: Ask politely with 본관이 어디세요? A homonym 본관 also means 'main building.'

추분.x: After the autumn equinox, the nights get longer and longer.

사랑방.m: sarangbang (the master's study and guest room in a hanok); gathering place
사랑방.x: Grandpa chatted with guests in the sarangbang.
사랑방.e: Not 'love room': this 사랑 is a Sino word for outer quarters, unrelated to native 사랑 (love).
사랑방.t: Figuratively it means a local hangout, e.g., 동네 사랑방 for a neighborhood gathering spot.

이전투구.m: a mudslinging fight, a dirty and ugly struggle
이전투구.x: The election is turning into a mudslinging fight.
이전투구.e: Literally 'dogs fighting in a muddy field'.
이전투구.t: Common in political news; 진흙탕 싸움 is the everyday equivalent.

전가하다.m: to shift (blame or burden) onto someone, to pass the buck
전가하다.x: Don't shift the blame for your mistakes onto others.
전가하다.e: Literally 'transfer and pass off' — the second syllable originally meant marrying a daughter off into another family, hence sending something over to someone else.
전가하다.t: Fixed collocation: 책임을 전가하다 or 부담을 전가하다.

타파하다.m: to break down, to abolish, to do away with (customs, prejudice)
타파하다.x: We must do away with outdated customs.

살뜰하다.ex: 어머니는 적은 월급으로 살림을 살뜰하게 꾸려 가셨어요.
살뜰하다.x: My mother managed the household thriftily on a small salary.
살뜰하다.e: Two kinds of care: careful with money, and attentive to people (살뜰히 챙기다).

애꿎다.ex: 화가 난다고 애꿎은 동생한테 소리 지르지 마세요.
애꿎다.x: Don't yell at your innocent little brother just because you're angry.
애꿎다.e: Almost always 애꿎은 + noun: the innocent bystander who takes the hit.

애오라지.x: He has lived thinking solely of his family.
애오라지.e: An old native adverb that survives mostly in literature and formal writing.
애오라지.t: Very literary; in conversation use 오로지 or 오직 instead.

금본위제.x: The U.S. effectively abandoned the gold standard in 1971.
금본위제.e: Literally 'system with gold as the base unit of value.'
